# Text and encoding

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Decode UTF-8 bytes from untrusted, remote or external input with a strict decoder that throws on invalid bytes, such as `new UTF8Encoding(false, throwOnInvalidBytes: true)`. Don't use the default `Encoding.UTF8`.** `Encoding.UTF8` silently puts replacement characters in place of invalid bytes. Corrupt input is hidden, and the code carries on with the wrong content. *Check:* Look for `Encoding.UTF8.GetString` (or `[Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString` in PowerShell) on request bodies, tokens, files or other bytes the code didn't produce itself. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #331</sub>
- **Decode unpadded base64url text, such as stored ciphertext or token segments, with one shared strict decoder built on `NCode.Base64Url`. Don't use `Convert.FromBase64String`, a lenient decoder, or a hand-written decoder in each implementation. Empty or invalid ciphertext throws `CryptographicException`, and a destination that is too short throws `ArgumentException`.** A single strict decoder rejects padding and illegal characters the same way everywhere, with the same exception and message. Lenient or duplicated decoders accept malformed input and drift apart. *Check:* Look for `Convert.FromBase64String`, ad hoc `-`/`_` substitution, or a custom base64url loop on base64url data. Also look for key-wrapping or ciphertext code that throws a different exception type for malformed input. <sub>Identity ADR-1260; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, decode a base64url segment into a buffer sized exactly by `Base64Url.GetByteCountForDecode` (for example one rented from a pool), and use the whole buffer. Don't slice it by `bytesWritten`.** `NCode.Base64Url` throws `FormatException` on invalid input, so a decode that succeeds fills the buffer exactly. Over-allocating and then slicing is extra code that suggests the decode is lenient. *Check:* Look for base64url decode buffers sized by a guess such as `length * 3 / 4` and then sliced by `bytesWritten`. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Always pass an explicit strict encoding to text APIs. Don't call an overload that picks an implicit encoding. This includes passing the codebase's strict UTF-8 encoding as `contentEncoding` to every `Results.Content`, `Results.Text`, `TypedResults.Content` and `TypedResults.Text` call.** An implicit or framework-default encoding is lenient and hides the conversion from review, so the response or file may not use the required strict UTF-8. *Check:* Look for `StreamReader`/`StreamWriter`, `File.ReadAllText`/`WriteAllText`, content helpers, and `Results`/`TypedResults` `Content`/`Text` calls that have no encoding argument. *Note:* The maintainer confirmed that the `Results`/`TypedResults` part also applies to test-only hosts, so report it in test code as well. For the exemption, see the rule about `HttpResponse.WriteAsync(string)`. <sub>Identity ADR-1266; Identity outcomes of #590</sub>
- **Don't report `HttpResponse.WriteAsync(string)` as a missing-encoding or lenient-encoding violation.** It is allowed on purpose: the ASP.NET Core request-delegate generator emits it, so banning it would make generated code fail. *Check:* Before reporting a missing-encoding finding, confirm the call isn't `HttpResponse.WriteAsync(string)`. If it is, the call is exempt. <sub>Identity ADR-1266</sub>
- **Encode text to bytes with a strict (throwing) UTF-8 encoding before hashing it for an integrity value, such as a CSP script hash. Don't use `Encoding.UTF8`.** The hash must match exactly the bytes the browser or verifier sees. `Encoding.UTF8` silently replaces invalid characters such as lone surrogates, which produces a hash of different content. *Check:* Look for hash or hash-source code that calls `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` on the hashed text. <sub>Identity ADR-1256</sub>
- **In production code, turn a date or time string into a CLR value only through the codebase's shared date-coercion helper. Don't hand-roll `DateTime.TryParse`, `DateTimeOffset.TryParse` or `ParseExact`. Parse a string as a date only where it is declared to be one, and never to sniff whether an arbitrary string looks like a date.** With one policy, every package accepts the same formats and gets the same values. Lenient sniffing turns strings such as "1.2" or "10:30" into dates and rewrites them. *Check:* Look for new `DateTime.Parse/TryParse`, `DateTimeOffset.Parse/TryParse` or `ParseExact` calls where a shared coercion helper exists, and for date parsing applied to untyped strings or claims. *Note:* The rule covers production code. Test projects may parse dates directly to build fixtures. <sub>Identity ADR-1122; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Parse an instant from text as a `DateTimeOffset` with the invariant culture. Treat a zone-less value as UTC (`DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal`), keep an explicit offset, and let an out-of-range instant fail. Don't parse it as a `DateTime`.** `DateTime` parsing converts to machine-local time and clamps an out-of-range instant such as `0001-01-01T00:00:00+05:00`. The result is a wrong instant that depends on the machine, where the parse should have failed. *Check:* Look for `DateTime` parsing of timestamp text that has an offset or no zone, for parsing without the invariant culture, and for zone-less values handled without UTC assumption. <sub>Identity ADR-1122; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Format and parse machine-facing values with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` and an exact `NumberStyles` such as `Integer` or `Float`. Never use `NumberStyles.Any`. Also use the invariant culture for numeric, date and `TimeSpan` values interpolated into validation and violation messages.** Culture-dependent or permissive parsing accepts wrong values and gives different results on different machines. Invariant formatting makes messages read the same everywhere. *Check:* Look for `Parse`, `TryParse`, `ToString` or string interpolation on numbers, dates or `TimeSpan`s in wire formats, storage, configuration or validation messages without `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` (or `FormattableString.Invariant`), and for `NumberStyles.Any`. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1206</sub>
- **In production code, give a typed `System.Security.Claims.Claim` its value in the declared value type's XML Schema lexical form, for example `value.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` for `ClaimValueTypes.Integer`. Never use a culture-formatted value.** Mapping claims to JSON parses each value strictly in its declared type. A culture-formatted value such as "1,000" is not in that lexical space, so it goes out as a string instead of a number. *Check:* Look for `new Claim(..., x.ToString(), ClaimValueTypes.Integer/Double/...)` or interpolated numbers without the invariant culture. <sub>Identity ADR-1122; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Compare an opaque, case-significant key, such as a base64url id, hash or token, ordinally and verbatim. Case-fold only values that are defined to match case-insensitively.** Case-folding or culture-aware comparison of opaque keys produces false matches. *Check:* Look for `OrdinalIgnoreCase`, `ToLower`/`ToUpper`, `CurrentCulture` or `InvariantCulture` comparisons applied to ids, hashes or tokens. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Inside a password policy, count a password's length in Unicode code points (runes, for example `EnumerateRunes()`) of its NFC-normalized form, and check blocklists against the NFC form. Never truncate the password. Callers pass the password exactly as submitted and don't normalize it first.** NIST SP 800-63B-4 counts each code point as one character, so a surrogate pair is one character. The length must also be the length of what the store hashes. Otherwise a decomposed spelling passes as long enough or gets past a blocklist that lists the composed spelling, and truncation weakens the password. *Check:* Look for password length checks that use `string.Length` or UTF-16 units, or that run on un-normalized text. Also look for blocklist lookups on the submitted form, truncating or substringing a password, and callers that normalize before calling the policy. <sub>Identity ADR-1236; Identity ADR-1238</sub>
- **Append query parameters to a URL by percent-encoding each name and value with `Uri.EscapeDataString`. Join with `?`, or with `&` when the URL already has a query.** This follows RFC 3986 without needing an ASP.NET Core query helper, and it keeps any query the URL already has. *Check:* Look for query strings built by concatenation without `Uri.EscapeDataString`, and for code that always appends `?` even when the URL may already contain a query. <sub>Identity ADR-1285</sub>
- **In front-end code, encode an identifier placed in a URL path as a single segment with `encodeURIComponent`, and decode it with `decodeURIComponent` when parsing. Treat a blank id or a malformed encoding as matching no route.** Identifiers can contain any character, so they must round-trip safely, and invalid input must not resolve to a route. *Check:* Look for ids interpolated into paths without `encodeURIComponent`, parsing without `decodeURIComponent` or without catching its `URIError`, and blank ids that are still accepted. <sub>Identity ADR-1255</sub>
- **When writing a configured URL into output such as an HTML `href` or a response, validate it, then write the configured string itself. Use the parsed `Uri` only to validate and to derive values such as the origin.** `Uri.AbsoluteUri` and `Uri.ToString()` normalize the value. They can add a trailing slash and change case and escaping, so the output would no longer match the configured value byte for byte. Identifiers are carried as strings. *Check:* Look for `uri.AbsoluteUri` or `uri.ToString()` written into rendered markup or responses where the original configured string is available. <sub>Identity outcomes of #747</sub>
- **When parsing `Accept-Language` into locale preferences, order the entries by descending quality and drop the `*` wildcard and any entry with `q=0`.** The user agent's preferences must be read in their stated priority, and a `q=0` entry or the wildcard names no language to render. *Check:* Look for `Accept-Language` parsing that keeps header order regardless of q-values, or that passes `*` or `q=0` entries on as preferences. <sub>Identity ADR-1402</sub>
- **A regular expression meant to match within a single line uses `[ \t]` and `[^\r\n]` rather than `\s` and `.` wherever a newline must not match.** `\s` matches newlines, and `.` can too depending on the options, so multi-line input can match a pattern written for one line. *Check:* Look for single-line patterns that use `\s` between tokens or `.*` on input that may contain line breaks, where the regex options aren't stated. <sub>project-template outcomes of #146</sub>
- **When code scans Markdown, for example for headings, follow the CommonMark fence rule. A fence opens on a run of three or more backticks or tildes. It closes only on a line holding nothing but a run of the same character at least as long as the opening run. A fence that is never closed runs to the end of the file.** If one flag toggles on any fence marker, mixed or longer markers make headings inside code samples count, or cause real headings after a sample to be skipped. *Check:* Look for fence detection that toggles a single flag on any ``` or ~~~ line, ignores the length or character of the opening run, or ignores text after the closing run. <sub>project-template outcomes of #142</sub>
- **Write bytes that hold valid UTF-8 text as `u8` string literals, and declare a fixed protocol label (such as an HKDF info, purpose or prefix) as a `static ReadOnlySpan<byte>` property that returns a `u8` literal. Use explicit byte arrays only for invalid UTF-8 or error-case data.** `u8` literals are clearer, cost nothing per call, and pass straight to span APIs. Encoding a constant string at runtime is wasted work and hides the bytes. *Check:* Look for `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("literal")`, `const string` labels encoded before use in crypto or wire formats, and hand-written byte arrays of valid text. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **In new code, parse JSON with `JsonElement.Parse` rather than `JsonDocument.Parse` or `JsonDocument.ParseValue` where a `JsonElement` is all that is needed.** `JsonElement.Parse` leaves no disposable document to own, and the codebase is moving off the older parsing APIs. *Check:* Look for new `JsonDocument.Parse` or `JsonDocument.ParseValue` calls in the diff where `JsonElement.Parse` would do. <sub>Identity review of #382</sub>
- **Server-rendered pages write the selected locale's tag into the `lang` attribute of the `html` element. Client-side code renders in that page language and doesn't negotiate its own language from `navigator.languages`.** If the client chose its own language, pages that work without JavaScript would stay in one language, the first frame would flash another, and the document's `lang` wouldn't match what the user reads. *Check:* Look for rendered HTML documents without a server-set `lang`, and for front-end code that picks its locale from `navigator.language` or `navigator.languages` instead of the document's `lang`. <sub>Identity ADR-1402</sub>
- **Localize server-rendered text that hosts may extend with registered message records that a host can add or replace through dependency injection. Don't use `.resx` satellite-assembly resources for it.** A host can't add a language or change wording in satellite assemblies, but it can replace or extend a small registered message record. *Check:* Look for new `.resx` files or `IStringLocalizer` resource lookups added for end-user text that hosts are meant to extend. <sub>Identity ADR-1402</sub>
- **Save files as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, with LF line endings, following the repository's `.editorconfig`. Don't let a change add a BOM to a file. This includes files generated by tools such as `dotnet ef migrations add`: strip the BOM from them before committing.** UTF-8 without a BOM and with LF line endings is the base file convention in every repository. A BOM or CRLF added by an editor or a scaffolding tool changes the file for no reason and adds noise to diffs. *Check:* Look in the diff for a U+FEFF added before line 1 of a file (including newly scaffolded migration, designer and model snapshot files), for CRLF line endings, and for formatting that contradicts `.editorconfig`. <sub>Identity project-template.instructions.md; identity-platform project-template.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #598; Identity ADR-1180</sub>
- **In test projects, write string literals whose Unicode normalization form matters with escapes, for example `"café"` (composed) and `"café"` (decomposed). Never paste the characters.** An editor may normalize a pasted character, which silently changes what the test exercises. *Check:* Look for literal accented, precomposed or combining characters in test strings for normalization-sensitive behavior. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md; Identity csharp-tests.instructions.md</sub>
